<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

"Everything exists as tested parts on main; this plan is WIRING, deliberately lean (Jordan: 'don't overbake it'). Add a root via the CLI -> daemon snapshots+enqueues -> job runner scans (pure scanner) -> enrichment jobs summarize+embed through the provider registry (fake in CI, Azure live) -> semantic search returns ranked hits in the workshop-004 envelope. Proof: fs3 indexes ITSELF and answers queries. Authorities: workshops 002 (schema, landed), 003 (query surface - v1 slice only), 004 (envelope - v1 slice only); daemon-worker-architecture.md incl. its queued decisions, two of which this plan settles small: retry = 3 attempts with not_before backoff; re-queue-while-running = accept reconciler latency."

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- One end-to-end path: add path -> scanned -> enriched -> searchable, all through the daemon (single writer, PRD 20).
- Deterministic CI proof with the fake provider; recorded live run with Azure via the registry.
- First slice of the query surface (semantic search + core filters) in the workshop-004 envelope with next_action/fix.
- Idempotence: re-scanning an unchanged repo costs zero enrichment (content-addressing doing its job).

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- File watcher (daemon plan proper - doctrine locked, not wired here).
- Conversations, text/regex modes, full filter set, MCP, doctor, docs get/list.
- Concurrency combinator crate (inline semaphore/batching is enough for v1; combinator remains a roster row).
- Cross-platform release/CI (reqs 46-48) and s002 phase-2 docker paving (parallel, ox).

<a id="execution-guardrails"></a>

## Execution Guardrails

- Authorities bind: workshops 002/003/004 + fs3-architecture.md; contradiction = stop-and-ask.
- Only the daemon writes PG (PRD 20); the CLI never opens a pool.
- Enrichment stays keyed by raw_hash (D2) - anything keyed by element id is drift.
- Fake provider for all CI; keyed Azure only for the recorded live run.
- Shared-tree commit discipline per ruling 2026-08-26 (file-scoped adds, push-first, scoped fmt).
